subject: Labeling ranges of values on an axis

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Labeling ranges of values on an axis
parts:
Hi,
I have an x-axis that is broken into ranges. I am trying to using `scale_x_continuous` to nicely format these ranges, but I can’t get exactly what I want.

Below are the two versions I have come up with. What I would like is Version 1, but not having major lines plotted on top of the Range labels (but continue to keep them with “|”). Version 2 is ok, but I was hoping to have the text outside the plot area - is there a way to do that with `annotate`?

Or is there a better way to do this all-together?

dta <- data.frame(x = 1:12, y = 1:12)
library(ggplot2)

# Version 1
ggplot(dta) +
geom_line(aes(x, y)) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10), labels = c("Range 1", "|", "Range 2", "|", "Range 3"))

# Version 2
ggplot(dta) +
geom_line(aes(x, y)) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(4, 8), labels = c("|", "|")) +
annotate("text", x = c(2, 6, 10), y = -1, label = paste("Range", 1:3))

Thanks for your help!
Doug

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Labeling ranges of values on an axis
parts:
Hi Doug:

Here are a couple of ideas that don't require messing around with
annotate() or grid graphics to place text grobs outside the plot
region. The first is to get rid of the x-axis ticks and draw a couple
of segments inside the plot region. This is OK but it's a bit awkward
to have two sets of axis ticks of different size and in different
directions. The other idea is to fill color the plot background
differently for each range, which IMO looks a bit better.

# (1) Add segments

scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2, 6, 10),
labels = paste("Range", 1:3)) +
theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4))) +
geom_segment(aes(x = c(4, 8), xend = c(4, 8), y = c(1, 1),
yend = c(0, 0))) +
scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 12.5))

#(2) Add background rectangles
ggplot(dta) +
theme_bw() +
geom_rect(aes(xmin = c(0, 4, 8), xmax = c(4, 8, 12),
ymin = rep(0, 3), ymax = rep(Inf, 3),
fill = c("red", "blue", "green")), alpha = 0.2) +
geom_line(aes(x, y)) +
scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(2, 6, 10),
labels = paste("Range", 1:3)) +
theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4))) +
scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 12.5)) +
scale_fill_discrete(guide = "none")


I understand your dilemma, but I think fixing the problem at the axis
level would entail an excursion into grid graphics. These may not be
what you had in mind, but if the idea is to differentiate among
different regions of values, the second approach has some appeal. You
could, for example, create a legend for the fill color, eliminating
the need to specify the range in the x-axis, but there are a number of
options available regarding labeling, including your second example,
so pick what works best for you.

Dennis

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: Labeling ranges of values on an axis
parts:
Hey Dennis,
Thanks for your suggestions, these are very helpful. In my real data set, I was already planning on coloring the lines on a different variable, so you Version 2, while I like, will not work in this case. However, your Version 1 use of `geom_segment` inspired a new idea that I think I will use - which is basically to make up the major axis lines on my own.

ggplot(dta) +
geom_segment(aes(x = c(4, 8), xend = c(4, 8), y = c(Inf, Inf), yend = c(-Inf, -Inf)), size = 0.75, color = "grey") +
geom_line(aes(x, y)) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10), labels = c("Range 1", "|", "Range 2", "|", "Range 3")) +
theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

Thanks again!

Doug
